K02 A-1 lib.rs:282: index_text.parse::<i64>() runs only after split_selector (175-183) and is_index (187-190) have checked that the text is an optional '-' followed by >=1 ASCII digits, after Key::parse (272), after the existing-key check (273-275) and after the list check (279-281). So the only error it can discard is i64 overflow (|index| >= 2^63). Such an index cannot select an element of any list, so IndexOutOfRange is exactly SPEC's `index out of range` for it. Observed: hosts[99999999999999999999] and hosts[-99999999999999999999] give `error: index out of range`; port[99999999999999999999] (an int) gives `not of type list`; nope[...] gives `no such key`.

K02 A-4 lib.rs:182: selector() maps every i64 parse failure to IndexOutOfRange. lookup() calls selector() at line 276 BEFORE Key::parse, the store lookup (280) and the list check (286). So a G2-valid index outside the i64 range (SPEC Element selectors: 'The index is an integer in the form of G2', so the syntax is legal) gives `index out of range` even when the key is not defined or its value is not a list. SPEC requires `no such key `<key>`` or `key `<key>` is not of type list` there, since 'index out of range' applies only to an index that does not select an element OF THE LIST. Changing only the flagged expression so that an overflowing index becomes i64::MIN/MAX (which cannot select an element) defers the error to its proper place and fixes the output.
